- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ -0.33) and prices are falling, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward more aggressively.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., 70.93→71.17), overshooting by 1–2% in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizon; if forecast is >1.5% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 0.5–1.0%.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; apply downward correction at 10–15 day mark if sentiment drops below 0.33.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to underestimate late-period spikes (e.g., 72.52); add 0.5–1.0% buffer if sentiment is bullish and price is trending up.
